reconcile.note: John Gill restricts 'the dead know not anything' to bodily senses, while holding that souls remain conscious and even better informed after death.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll holds that the Old Testament teaches death ends all, a claim the New Testament's bodily resurrection cannot honestly reconcile.

quotes.text: If the Old Testament proves anything, it is that death ends all. And the New Testament, by basing immortality on the resurrection of the body, but "keeps the word of promise to our ear and breaks it to our hope."
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (Ingersoll's Rejoinder to Judge Jeremiah S. Black) (1881), on Ecclesiastes 9:5 and Isaiah 26:19.

sides.verseText: For the living know that they will die, but the dead don't know anything, neither do they have any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

sides.snippet: Your dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise.
sides.verseText: Your dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is [as] the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast forth the dead.
